input.baseline: Twice a week, about 5 km each. My easy 5 km takes 35–37 minutes. Longest run was 7 km.

asked.question: Do you have a finish time in mind?
Why does it matter?
asked.answer: To finish it with my friends

baselineMeasurements.sourceQuote: Twice a week, about 5 km each.
Twice a week, about 5 km each.

options.rationale: A patient 20 week build from 10 km a week and a 7 km longest run, adding about 10% a week with easy running so you can reach the half marathon start line with your friends.
assumptions: No finish time target, success is finishing
3 to 4 training days a week, 3 in the first two weeks
Easy pace stays 7:00-7:24 per km
Weekly volume grows gradually with easier weeks if tired

sessions.title: Easy run 4 km
sessions.descriptiveGuide: Run 4 km easy and smooth. Focus on relaxed shoulders and short steps, staying at a pace where you can talk.

targets.progressMeasure: Log time and effort from 1 to 10.

sessions.title: Easy run 4 km

input.baseline: 60 kg for 5 reps, 3 sets. I lift 3 days a week, with a rack and a spotter.

baselineMeasurements.sourceQuote: 3 sets. I lift 3 days a week

options.rationale: A patient climb from 60 kg to 80 kg for 5 reps, adding small loads about every 1 to 2 weeks, with lighter weeks built in to keep progress sustainable.
assumptions: You keep lifting about 3 days a week with a rack and spotter
Load rises in small steps of 2.5 kg when all reps feel solid
Some weeks may repeat a load if reps slow down
Progress is not guaranteed and depends on recovery

phases.title: Steady load climb

phases.progressCheck: Complete 3 sets of 5 reps at 75 kg, or 5 reps top set at 75 kg

sessions.title: Bench press 3x5 at 60 kg
sessions.descriptiveGuide: Warm up with a few lighter sets, then do 3 working sets of 5 reps at 60 kg. Rest fully between sets and use your spotter. Stop each set with a rep or two left in reserve.

targets.progressMeasure: Log whether all 15 reps were smooth and note how hard the last set felt

sessions.title: Bench press 3x5 at 60 kg
sessions.descriptiveGuide: Warm up, then do 3 working sets of 5 reps at 60 kg with a steady lowering phase and a brief pause on the chest. Use your spotter and rest fully between sets.

targets.progressMeasure: Log reps completed and rate effort of the last set from 1 to 10

sessions.title: Bench press 3x5 at 60 kg
sessions.descriptiveGuide: Warm up, then do 3 working sets of 5 reps at 60 kg. Aim for even bar speed on every rep. Keep the spotter ready and rest fully between sets.

targets.effort: moderate, 1 to 2 reps left in reserve
targets.progressMeasure: Log whether the last set felt easier than on Monday

sessions.title: Bench press 3x5 at 62.5 kg
sessions.descriptiveGuide: Warm up, then do 3 working sets of 5 reps at 62.5 kg, the first small step up. Use your spotter, keep form tight and rest fully between sets.

targets.effort: moderate to hard, 1 to 2 reps left in reserve
targets.progressMeasure: Log how many of the 15 reps were completed with good form

sessions.title: Bench press 3x5 at 60 kg
sessions.descriptiveGuide: A steady session at 60 kg. Do 3 working sets of 5 reps with controlled lowering and a spotter. Use it to consolidate the new load from Monday.

targets.progressMeasure: Log bar speed and any form breakdown on the final reps

sessions.title: Bench press 3x5 at 62.5 kg
sessions.descriptiveGuide: Warm up, then do 3 working sets of 5 reps at 62.5 kg. Keep form tight, use your spotter and rest fully between sets.

targets.effort: moderate to hard, 1 to 2 reps left in reserve
targets.progressMeasure: Log whether all 15 reps were completed and compare with Monday

options.rationale: Four bench days a week with one heavy, one volume and two lighter days, adding small loads steadily from 60 kg toward 80 kg for 5 reps.

Rack and spotter are available every session
Load rises about 1 to 2.5 kg a week on the heavy day
Plan is adjusted if reps slow down or form breaks

phases.title: Steady load climb
phases.progressCheck: Heavy day reaches 72.5 kg for 3x5, and light days stay clean.

phases.title: Heavier work
phases.progressCheck: Complete 75 kg for 3x5 or 77.5 kg for 2 sets of 5.

sessions.title: Heavy day 3x5 at 60 kg
sessions.descriptiveGuide: Warm up with the empty bar and two lighter sets. Then 3 sets of 5 at 60 kg with the spotter ready. Keep shoulder blades tight and control the descent.

targets.effort: Moderately hard, 1 to 2 reps left in reserve
targets.progressMeasure: Log the reps for each set and how fast the last rep moved.

sessions.title: Light day 3x5 at 55 kg
sessions.descriptiveGuide: Warm up lightly, then 3 sets of 5 at 55 kg. Focus on a pause at the chest and smooth, steady reps. This is a recovery day for the chest.

targets.effort: Easy to moderate, 3 or more reps left in reserve
targets.progressMeasure: Note how easy each set felt from 1 to 10.

sessions.title: Top day 3x5 at 62.5 kg
sessions.descriptiveGuide: Warm up with ramping sets. Do 3 sets of 5 at 62.5 kg with the spotter. Stop a set if the bar slows a lot or form breaks.

targets.effort: Hard but controlled, 1 rep left in reserve
targets.progressMeasure: Log whether all 15 reps were completed at 62.5 kg.

sessions.title: Technique day 3x5 at 57.5 kg
sessions.descriptiveGuide: Warm up, then 3 sets of 5 at 57.5 kg. Keep the same bar path each rep, feet planted, and lower under control for two seconds.

targets.effort: Moderate, 2 or more reps left in reserve
targets.progressMeasure: Note if the bar path and the touch point stayed the same.

sessions.title: Volume day 4x5 at 60 kg
sessions.descriptiveGuide: Warm up, then 4 sets of 5 at 60 kg. The extra set builds work capacity. Keep rests steady and stay tight through every rep.

targets.effort: Moderately hard, 1 to 2 reps left in reserve
targets.progressMeasure: Log reps per set and whether the fourth set slowed down.

sessions.title: Light day 3x5 at 55 kg
sessions.descriptiveGuide: Warm up lightly, then 3 sets of 5 at 55 kg with crisp, controlled reps and a short pause on the chest. Keep it easy to aid recovery.

targets.effort: Easy to moderate, 3 or more reps left in reserve
targets.progressMeasure: Note how easy each set felt from 1 to 10.

sessions.title: Top day 3x5 at 65 kg
sessions.descriptiveGuide: Warm up with ramping sets, then 3 sets of 5 at 65 kg with the spotter ready. If the last set is missed, repeat 65 kg next week.

targets.effort: Hard but controlled, 1 rep left in reserve
targets.progressMeasure: Log reps completed at 65 kg and any spotter help needed.

sessions.title: Technique day 3x5 at 57.5 kg
sessions.descriptiveGuide: Warm up, then 3 sets of 5 at 57.5 kg. Lower for two seconds, touch the same spot on the chest, and press smoothly without bouncing.

targets.effort: Moderate, 2 or more reps left in reserve
targets.progressMeasure: Note whether every rep looked the same as the first.

cases.title: First half marathon, one day a week (mine)

input.baseline: I run 3 km once a week at an easy pace.

asked.question: Do you have a finish time in mind?

coachNote.message: A first half marathon needs at least 3 runs a week to build safely, so both plans use 3 days. Starting from 3 km, the patient road takes longer, but it gets you to the line.

baselineMeasurements.sourceQuote: I run 3 km once a week at an easy pace.
I run 3 km once a week at an easy pace.

options.rationale: A patient build from 3 km a week to a first half marathon, with three easy-effort days a week and gradual increases.
assumptions: No injuries or interruptions in the coming months
Three running days every week
All running stays at an easy, conversational effort
No finish time target, so success is completing the distance

phases.title: Build the habit
phases.progressCheck: Run 3 days a week with the longest run at 4-5 km, all at easy effort.

phases.title: Extend the long run
phases.progressCheck: Longest run reaches 8-10 km and weekly total about 18 km, still able to talk.

phases.title: Build endurance
phases.progressCheck: Longest run reaches 14-16 km, with easy effort and normal recovery.

phases.title: Peak long runs
phases.progressCheck: Complete one long run of 18-19 km and feel able to continue at easy effort.

phases.title: Taper and race
phases.progressCheck: Reduce volume in week 27, arrive fresh, and complete 21.1 km in week 28.

targets.progressMeasure: Log the total time and whether the last km felt as easy as the first.

sessions.descriptiveGuide: Run 2 km at an easy effort as a shorter day between longer runs. Keep it comfortable and smooth.

targets.progressMeasure: Note any soreness from the 3 km run two days earlier.

sessions.title: Easy 2 km run
sessions.descriptiveGuide: Run 2 km at an easy conversational effort. Finish the week feeling fresh rather than tired.

options.rationale: Three runs a week from the start and a steady rise of about 10% a week builds toward 21 km in 20 weeks, with a taper at the end. No target time is set, so success means finishing.
assumptions: No injuries or health limits that stop regular running
3 to 4 run days a week can be kept up for 20 weeks
Weekly distance rises about 10%, with an easier week now and then
Finishing is the goal, so no pace target is set
